evidence.text: Q4 guide risk from the iPhone. Nikkei (2026-10-09) reports Apple cut October component orders for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max by at least 15% (15-20% per one executive). Loop Capital (2026-10-21) puts the 2H26 cut at about 13M units and the December-quarter shipments at 79M against 85M. Amkor's Communications line is 42% of sales, and in July management had already guided it down high single digits in Q3, said Q4 would see 'a little bit of softness' and 'no significant H2 lift'. The Q4 revenue consensus of about $2.05B (flat on Q3) was set before the cut. Amkor's own Q4 2025 guide was -8% on Q3 ($1.775-1.875B against $1.99B).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: Q3 revenue guide of $1.95-2.05B against about $2.09B consensus took the stock -24.74% despite a Q2 beat. October 2025: Q4 guided down about 8% QoQ, stock -3.07%. February 2025: weak Q1 and an iOS socket loss, stock -11.33%. Guidance misses have moved this name the most.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The stock went from $55 on Oct 2 (Form 4 sale price) to $46.92 on Oct 13 and $38 today, and the skew pays for downside. Amkor is not named in the Nikkei story. The residual risk is that the Q4 consensus snapshot was not cut to match; B. Riley's 'in line' preview suggests the street expects the computing ramp to cover it. If it were fully priced, the Q4 consensus would sit below Q3 the way it did in 2025.
evidence.independence: Loop Capital note via MacRumors, 2026-10-21 (https://macrumors.com/2026/10/21/loop-capital-cuts-apple-rating-over-iphone-sales-outlook). Management's own July commentary on Q4 comms softness (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2939619). Q4 2025 guide (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1047127/000104712725000187/amkr9302025erex-991.htm). Net of the rest of the company: computing (22% of sales, guided +~30% QoQ in Q3, HDFO CPU and NVIDIA ramps) and auto/industrial (22%) must grow roughly 8-10% QoQ to keep Q4 flat. That is plausible, so this finding is sized net and small.

evidence.text: Peer read-through for the reported quarter. ASE's ATM (assembly, test and materials) revenue for Q3 2026 was NT$151.5B, +20.1% QoQ (+18.7% in USD, +40.6% YoY). In July ASE guided ATM +11-13% QoQ, so the largest OSAT beat its own Q3 guide by about 7-8 points. Amkor's Q3 consensus of $2.04B implies +7.5% QoQ, near the top of its $1.95-2.05B guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue $1.898B against a $1.75-1.85B guide (+2.6% above the top) and gross margin 16.8% against a 14.5-15.5% guide, and the stock fell 24.74% on the guide. This name sells reported-quarter beats.
evidence.why_not_priced: ASE's September revenue was public on Oct 12, yet AMKR fell from about $47 to $38 afterward, so the market did not carry the OSAT-strength read across. If it had, the Q3 consensus would sit above the top of guide rather than at it. The caveat is that ASE's beat is heavily AI/CoWoS and SPIL-driven, while Amkor's Q3 has an iOS/Android drag.
evidence.independence: ASE's Q3 guide of ATM +11-13% QoQ is from its Q2 results coverage (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/ase-technology-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-30/); that figure comes from one source in the search summary. TSMC's Q3 beat is a separate finding.

evidence.text: Amkor's own guide-beat record. Q2 2026 revenue was $1.898B against a $1.75-1.85B guide, gross margin 16.8% against 14.5-15.5%, EPS $0.70 against $0.42-0.52. Q1 2026 revenue was $1.685B against a $1.65B consensus. Utilization was in the high 70s in Q2, and management said utilization excluding Korea-to-Vietnam transit assets was 'pretty high'. A similar beat would put Q3 at about $2.05-2.10B and gross margin above 19.5%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 beat was sold (-24.74%) because of the guide. Q1 2026 was a small beat with stock -5.63%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The consensus already sits at the top of guide and the EPS consensus of $0.78-0.79 is near the guide's upper half. Only an above-top beat is unpriced.
evidence.independence: The Q1 2026 8-K for the Q2 guide (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001047127/000104712726000017/amkr3312026erex-991.htm). This rests on Amkor's own documents, separate from the ASE finding, although both lean toward a Q3 beat.

evidence.text: Auto/industrial counterparty strength. Texas Instruments reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-21: revenue $6.05-6.06B against $5.91B consensus (+28% YoY, +11% QoQ), analog +32%. Its Q4 guide is $5.80-6.30B (midpoint about flat QoQ, against TI's usual seasonal decline). Amkor's automotive, industrial and other line is 22% of sales and was guided +mid-single digits QoQ in Q3.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved Amkor print where auto/industrial alone moved the stock. In February 2025 auto weakness was cited alongside the iOS socket loss (-11.33%).
evidence.why_not_priced: TI spoke after Amkor last guided, and AMKR has fallen since with the sector. This is a proxy: TI's own packaging is largely in-house, so transmission to Amkor's auto line is inferred, not confirmed by a direct counterparty.
evidence.independence: 247wallst TI Q3 card (https://247wallst.com/cards/texas-instruments-q3-2026-earnings-txn-01m5g1n6r3j45hcsgta6qbhjgw). Proxy only.

evidence.text: On 2026-10-21 Amkor announced a new $1.3B multi-year agreement with NVIDIA to expand advanced packaging capacity in South Korea, bringing NVIDIA agreements across Korea and Arizona to $3B. It also plans to raise interposer wafer capacity by more than 300% by end-2028. That gives the call material to support a Computing-led Q4 guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July NVIDIA $1.5B Arizona deal (announced 2026-07-23) did not stop the -24.74% post-print move. After the 2026-10-21 Korea deal the stock went from $41.94 (Oct 20) to $39.30 (Oct 23), so the market faded it.
evidence.why_not_priced: Public and faded. What remains is whether management quantifies Q4 computing growth or NVIDIA prepayment timing on the call (in July the prepayment was said to arrive in 2027). If it were priced as a growth driver, the stock would not have fallen after the announcement.
evidence.independence: July NVIDIA partnership (https://evertiq.com/design/2026-07-24-nvidia-amkor-sign-15-billion-chip-packaging-agreement) and management's July 'computing nearly +30% QoQ' guide (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2939619).

evidence.text: Capex and financing. On 2026-09-08 Amkor expanded its Arizona campus to about $12B (Phase 2, +60,000 m2 cleanroom, construction late 2027 to 2029) 'because customer commitments exceeded Phase 1'. 2026 capex is $2.5-3.0B against H1 PP&E payments of $688M. Capex payable was $621M, and $1.15B of 0% converts were issued in May 2026. Management warned that the US manufacturing burden will weigh on margins in 2027-2028. A 2027 capex or margin framework may appear on the call.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. The February 2026 Kim-family secondary (10M shares at $48.75) cost about 6-7% intraday, a different item.
evidence.why_not_priced: The spend is public. The answer to 'what does the money buy' is customer commitments (NVIDIA prepayments, Arizona and Korea), so it funds visible demand. The sign is zero, with downside only if a 2027 capex guide lands well above the street.
evidence.independence: The CFO's July capex and margin comments (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2939619) and the NVIDIA Korea deal (shares the NVIDIA entity with the finding above; not counted twice).

evidence.text: Much of the October drawdown is sector beta. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Two up moves in seven prints, +18.13% (July 2025) and +1.79% (February 2026). The +18% came after a weak period, when guidance cleared the bar.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a statement about what is priced. The skew and put/call show the market is already braced for a bad guide. If the decline were company-specific, the B. Riley preview would not call Q3 and Q4 in line. Small, because a drawdown is not by itself a reason to bounce.
evidence.independence: Bloomberg on the SOX $1T+ loss (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-14/chip-stocks-set-to-erase-1-trillion-in-value-as-rout-deepens) and Tickeron's 30-day decomposition (https://tickeron.com/blogs/amkor-technology-amkr-stock-falls-27-6-in-30-days-key-factors-and-outlook-20708/).

evidence.text: Android and memory headwinds in Communications. In July management cited memory supply constraints and Android revenue down about 20%, and expected continued Android weakness. IDC (via secondary outlets) projects 2026 smartphone units -16.7%, the steepest decline on record. This bears on the Q4 comms guide beyond the iPhone cut.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same comms line as the iPhone finding. The July guide miss (-24.74%) was partly comms-driven.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: management told the market in July, so this sits inside what the company already guided. The only residual is the worsening memory shortage since then, and the IDC figure comes from a secondary outlet.
evidence.independence: IndexBox on memory costs (https://www.indexbox.io/blog/apple-trims-iphone-18-pro-component-orders-as-memory-costs-surge/). Shares the comms line with the iPhone finding but rests on a different customer set (Android).

evidence.why_not_priced: Public since Oct 15 and the stock fell afterward with the sector. The transmission to Amkor's revenue is an inference (proxy), so this is sized small.

first_hunter_context.positioning_check: FINRA short interest was 32.63M shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 6.73 days to cover, up from 27.16M on 08-14 and 30.80M on 09-15 (https://equibles.com/stocks/glxy/shortinterest). That is 8.3% of total shares, but about 17% of the roughly 195M Class A shares, with insiders owning 51.5% (MarketBeat 2026-10-16). Part of this short is likely convert-arb hedging: the May 2026 resale prospectus registers 36.4M shares underlying exchangeable notes held by Linden, MMCAP, Voya and others. The 10-15 settlement is not yet published. Skew is -1.02 vol points (balanced, slight call bid) and put/call OI is 1.09. The straddle implies 12.9% and the event-implied move is 11.34%. The stock is -33% over 20 days and -62% from its 52-week high, sitting 5% above its 52-week low. The skew does not lean against a positive sign, and a crowded, rising short argues against sizing negatives large.

evidence.text: Q3 2026 crypto prices rose sharply: BTC +42.9% (about $58.5k to $83-86k), ETH about +57-71%, SOL about +48% ($80 to $118). Against Galaxy's Q2 Treasury & Corporate net digital asset and investment exposure of $1.16B, which posted -$42M adjusted gross profit in Q2 when BTC fell 14%, this implies a swing to a large segment gain, plausibly +$150-300M. That would put Q3 net income and EPS well above a consensus that still expects a loss of $0.06-$0.13.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 had ETH +66% and Treasury & Corporate adjusted gross profit of $408M, with net income $505M and adjusted EPS $1.12; the stock moved +8.1% close-to-close (baseline 2025-10-21). Q2 2026 beat on EPS (-$0.09 vs a -$0.36 or -$0.05 bar), but revenue missed, and the stock moved -13.89%. Q4 2025 was a mark-driven loss and the stock moved -16.87%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Every published bar still models a Q3 loss: -$0.06 (Benzinga, about 10-22) and -$0.13 (Earnings Whispers). The FY consensus is -$0.87 (MarketBeat 10-16). If the sell side had marked Q3 crypto, Q3 EPS estimates would be positive and well above zero. The stock has fallen 33% in 20 days on CoreWeave and AI-credit news, so the backward-looking mark is not what holders are trading.
evidence.independence: ETH +70.8% in Q3 2026 (https://phemex.com/news/article/ethereum-posts-strongest-quarterly-gain-since-q1-2021-with-708-q3-rise-98634) and SOL +48% (https://247wallst.com/investing/cryptocurrency/2026/10/02/how-high-can-solana-go-in-2026-after-a-48-quarter/). Q2 segment exposure is from the company's Q2 release (https://finviz.com/news/377387/galaxy-announces-second-quarter-2026-financial-results). This is a proxy: Galaxy has not disclosed Q3 holdings or hedges.

evidence.text: Q3 is the first full quarter of Helios Phase I. All 133 MW of critical IT load was in service by 30 June, and the company guided to about $80M of quarterly leasing revenue at a project-level adjusted EBITDA margin above 90% from Q3. In Q2 the Data Centers segment had $20M adjusted gross profit.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 was the first Helios revenue quarter: $20M adjusted gross profit and $11M adjusted EBITDA, and the stock moved -13.89%, driven by the revenue miss headline. There is no earlier history on this line.
evidence.why_not_priced: This sits inside company guidance and is largely priced. Its only incremental value is confirming that CoreWeave paid in full during a credit scare. If the market trusted that payment, GLXY would not have fallen in step with CoreWeave's bonds.
evidence.independence: StoneX notes Phase I delivered 133 MW in July and generated first revenue (https://theblock.co/news/markets/2026-10-19-galaxy-digital-glxy-stonex-buy-coreweave-helios-ai-data-center-421045). This shares the company document with the guidance.

evidence.text: CoreWeave, sole tenant for the first 800 MW at Helios, is under credit stress. Its stock fell about 25% in the week to 10-16, its 2031/2032 bond yields touched 15-16%, and its debt was $35.6-51.6B at June. Galaxy funded Phase II with $3.5B of 9.875% secured notes, so the call will be dominated by counterparty questions the release cannot settle.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior print with a tenant-credit scare. The stock fell about 30% in two weeks on this line before the print (Benzinga and The Block, 10-19).
evidence.why_not_priced: Most of this is priced: the stock is -33% over 20 days and options imply 11%. It stays a negative because the release can confirm CoreWeave paid but cannot remove the risk. Any hedged wording, schedule slip on Phase II (data halls from Q2 2027) or lease renegotiation in Q&A would add to it. If it were fully priced, GLXY would have stabilised as CoreWeave bonds rebounded on 10-15; it fell a further 15% after.
evidence.independence: Galaxy's sole-tenant exposure and StoneX's defence are at https://theblock.co/news/markets/2026-10-19-galaxy-digital-glxy-stonex-buy-coreweave-helios-ai-data-center-421045. Morgan Stanley cut its target $48 to $43 on AI-credit concerns (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/mara-riot-glxy-price-targets-cut-at-morgan-stanley-on-ai-credit-concerns-analyst-still-sees-over-100-upside/cZD6HOyRBn9). Financing check: the notes fund contracted Phase II ($10.4B minimum lease payments), so the financing is a ramp, not distress. The risk is the tenant, not the debt.

evidence.text: Citi upgraded GLXY to Buy on 10-13 (target $26 to $28), citing better Helios I economics and a possible Helios II tenant announcement within six months. A new, non-CoreWeave tenant announced with the print would directly answer the concentration fear.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The August 2025 CoreWeave Helios commitments moved the stock up materially. No print-day tenant announcement exists in the baseline history.
evidence.why_not_priced: The probability of an announcement inside this window is low, so it carries little in a stock priced on CoreWeave single-tenant risk. If a second tenant were expected, the stock would not trade 5% off its 52-week low.
evidence.independence: Galaxy has acquired land for a second Texas campus at McGregor (The Block, 10-19, same URL as finding 3). There is no tenant confirmation from any source.

evidence.text: Short interest rose from 27.2M shares (08-14) to 32.6M (09-30), 6.73 days to cover, about 17% of Class A shares. The stock fell a further 33% after that settlement, so a positive headline (a profit swing, CoreWeave paid) meets a crowded and growing short.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no measured squeeze on a past GLXY print. Days to cover was 3.7-4.8 at the prior prints, so it is higher now.
evidence.why_not_priced: Skew is balanced (-1.02), so options are not paying up for upside. If the squeeze were anticipated, calls would be bid over puts. Part of the short is exchangeable-note hedging, which does not need to cover, and that is why this is sized small.
evidence.independence: The exchangeable notes underlying 36.4M shares are in the resale prospectus (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001859392/000162828026037301/galaxy-resalesx3424b3.htm). That source cuts against this finding and is already netted into the size.

evidence.text: Galaxy's gross revenue tracks spot notional, and centralized-exchange spot volume fell 14% QoQ to $2.49T in Q3 2026 (Cryptorank). The $9.04B consensus is above Q2's $8.56B, so a revenue-miss headline is plausible again.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue was $8.56B against a $11.65-14.22B consensus, and headlines led with the miss; the stock moved -13.89% (CoinDesk 2026-08-05). In Q3 2025, record income outweighed revenue and the stock moved +8.1%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Headline algorithms read the revenue line on this name even though it is gross notional. If a miss were expected, the consensus would have been cut toward Q2's level.
evidence.independence: Q2 revenue miss and reaction: https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/08/05/galaxy-digital-shares-slip-5-after-second-quarter-results. This is a narrow proxy from a single secondary source; CCData's Q3 report was not found.

evidence.text: Direct peer Electrolux reported Q3 on 2026-10-23, after WHR last spoke on 2026-08-03. North American core-appliance demand fell ~5% in Q3, worse than the -3.4% WHR cited for Q2. Consumers are trading down to lower price points, and chemicals/resin were unhedged for the first time. On the other side, Electrolux NA sales rose +2% on price, the industry 'raised prices further', and promotions are 'far more reasonable' than the 'unreasonable price cuts' of Q4 2025. If WHR's larger price actions (>10% promotional in April plus ~4% list in July) track that, NA revenue would land near or above the -2.4% y/y consensus, while volume and mix weigh on the H2 guide. Net, this is a mixed read.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: NA revenue/margin has driven the last prints: Q2 (NA EBIT margin +240bp sequentially, FY reaffirmed) +13.8%; Q1 (demand -7.4%, guide cut, dividend suspended) -11.9%. Electrolux itself traded up as much as 12% intraday on this report and settled ~+2%.
evidence.why_not_priced: It landed three sessions before the print. WHR's Zacks NA revenue consensus ($2,657m, -2.4%) does not look updated for peer price realisation of +2% organic. If the market had read this as price discipline, WHR would not have kept making new lows into the print. If it had read it as demand deterioration, the skew would lean to puts, and it is flat at +0.86.
evidence.independence: Reuters via Euronext (https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/electrolux-reports-q3-core-profit-beat-says-north-america-weakness-persists, 2026-10-23) confirms NA +2% mainly on price and the trade-down. Same company and event, so not independent. The Brazil finding below also uses this report.

evidence.text: Competitors followed WHR's 2026 price increases through the summer, so WHR is less likely to lose share as its price lands in full in Q3: GE/Cafe/Monogram +7-11% (Jun 15), LG +6% (Jul 1), Bosch/Thermador +8-12% (Aug 1), KitchenAid +3.5-6.5% and Whirlpool ~+4% (Jul 9) on top of WHR's >10% April increase. WHR's Q2 call said only ~2/3 of the April increase landed in Q2, and that a Q3 NA margin step-up 'similar' to Q1-to-Q2 (+240bp) is 'absolutely critical'.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: pricing-led sequential NA margin gain plus a reaffirmed FY bought +13.8% despite an EPS miss.
evidence.why_not_priced: The price increases are public, but consensus Q3 EPS has been cut over the last 30 days and the stock is -13% month to date, which reads as a bet that price does not stick. If the market believed it would stick, the most-accurate EPS estimate would not sit near $0.20 against a $0.78 consensus. The finding lands inside what management guided (pricing was in the plan), so it is sized small.
evidence.independence: Retailer blog, not a primary document. Electrolux Q3 (a different source) says the industry 'raised prices further in the quarter' and that promotions are more rational. evidence.text: US retail appliance sell-through held up in the summer quarter. Best Buy's appliance comp was +0.2% (vs -9.2% a year ago), with large appliances growing, for the quarter ended 2026-08-01. Lowe's reported a seventh straight positive appliance comp in the quarter ended 2026-07-31, with ticket +2.3%. Both rest mostly on price and both periods overlap WHR's Q2 more than its Q3.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separable in the baseline. NA revenue was -1.5% in Q2 against a -3.4% industry and the stock rose +13.8%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The data is public and mostly pre-dates WHR's Q3. It is filed because it shows price is holding at retail, which the October estimate cuts discount. It is a proxy, so it is sized small.
evidence.independence: Lowe's Q2 call highlights (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/lowes-companies-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-19/, 2026-08-19), a separate retailer.

evidence.text: US hot-rolled coil reached $1,210-1,220/short ton in late September 2026 (Kallanish, 25 Sept), against $825-865 a year earlier, about +40%. Nucor raised its CSP $10/st every week through September and SMU's average approached $1,300/st. WHR said on the Q2 call that steel is 'at the high end of contracts', and Electrolux says steel is on yearly contracts now being renegotiated. That points to a 2027 cost headwind that will be visible in Q4 commentary and any early 2027 framing.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Raw materials were cited as a headwind in Q2 (stock +13.8% anyway). Not separable as a line.
evidence.why_not_priced: Sell-side cuts in October focus on demand and the 2026 EPS. If the market were pricing a 2027 steel reset, the 2027 street EPS ($3.33 per MarketBeat) would not still sit ~30% above the 2026 guide midpoint.
evidence.independence: Proxy: macro-to-company transmission that WHR has not quantified. Electrolux's Q3 call (different company) says steel contracts are yearly and being renegotiated in a volatile market, and that raw materials and logistics rose sharply.

evidence.text: US existing-home sales for September 2026 were 3.99m SAAR, -2.2% y/y. NAR said August and September were the two slowest months of the year and that rising mortgage rates in recent weeks mean fewer buyers qualify. This is a demand proxy for the discretionary and builder part of WHR's mix.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Housing is a recurring negative cited on prints. Q1 2026 (-11.9%) carried the demand collapse.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the release is public and the stock is -15% in 20 days. Filed as a small proxy. WHR says demand is mostly replacement-driven, which limits the transmission.
evidence.independence: Proxy. Electrolux's Q3 call reports US consumer confidence at a 10-year low and NA demand -5% (a different source on the same demand theme).

evidence.text: WHR's own Q2 release puts the FY guide out of reach on the cash line. H1 ongoing EPS was -$0.77 (Q1 -$0.56, Q2 -$0.21), so the $2.50-3.00 FY guide needs +$3.27-3.77 in H2. The ~$630m FY ongoing EBIT needs ~$520m in H2 against $106m in H1. FCF of 'over $300m' after H1 FCF of -$1,108m needs ~+$1.4bn in H2, yet management said it does not expect the usual heavy H2 working-capital release. Separately, the 10-Q shows supply-chain-financing payables falling from $772m to $629m, a working-capital drain. The street has already cut FY EPS to $2.25, so the EPS cut is expected. The unpriced swing is whether the FCF and the 'net debt below $5bn' target (from ~$5.8bn) are also cut, on an equity worth ~$1.7bn against that debt.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance decides this name. Q1 2026 FY cut plus dividend suspension: -11.9%. Q2 2026 EPS miss with the FY operating guide and FCF reaffirmed: +13.8%. Jul 2025 guide cut: -13.4%. Jan 2025 guide: -16.5%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The EPS shortfall is priced: the street FY sits below the guide's low end. The FCF and net-debt targets have not been publicly cut by the street in what I could find. If the market had priced an FCF cut on a ~3.4x net-debt-to-market-cap stub, the 25-delta skew would bid puts, and it is flat at +0.86.
evidence.independence: Q2 call (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-whirlpool-misses-q2-2026-estimates-but-shares-rise-93CH-4834496) for the 'no heavy H2 working-capital release' statement. 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000106640/000010664026000061/whr-20260630.htm) for supply-chain financing ($629m vs $772m) and the second-lien notes. All are company documents. Counterweight: maturities are cleared to 2028+ (second-lien notes due 2031/2034) and the $2bn ABL was undrawn at June 30, so this is a valuation risk, not a liquidity crisis. Shrunk for that and for the crowded short.

evidence.text: The bar was cut hard through October into the print. Zacks moved to Strong Sell on Oct 5 and its Q3 EPS consensus of $0.78 was cut over 30 days, with ESP -74.5% (most-accurate estimate ~$0.20). RBC cut its target to $22 (Oct 7), Citi to $32 from $48 (Oct 12) and Wells Fargo to $30 from $39 (Oct 16). The stock is -13.4% month to date and fell -5.5% on print day to $26.57, 0.4% above its 52-week low. Q2 showed the setup: a miss against a lowered bar with the FY operating guide reaffirmed bought +13.8%.

evidence.why_not_priced: The cuts are public. What is not settled is which bar the print is judged against ($0.20 / $0.78 / $0.93 / $1.01). A merely bad number can clear the lowest one, which the -5.5% print-day slide does not reflect. Capped small because the EPS bar is disputed.
evidence.independence: MarketBeat (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-whirlpool-whr-projected-to-post-earnings-on-monday-2026-10-19/) for the RBC/Citi cuts.
